study type: Review of existing data and policy proposal
exposure: Availability of data on timing and indication of Caesarean section
Availability of data on key population characteristics affecting CS risk
Availability of data on health system characteristics affecting CS risk
outcome: Availability of comparable health indicators to analyze CS rates and understand variability
cohort: Existing international databases (Eurostat, OECD, WHO) and national health information systems related to Caesarean section rates in Europe.
finding: A review of international databases confirmed wide variation in Caesarean section rates across Europe (16% to over 50%), but highlighted very limited data available to understand the reasons for these differences.
mod_finding: The study's primary finding confirmed significant variations in Caesarean section rates across Europe, emphasizing a lack of comparable data needed for effective surveillance and evaluation of this mode of birth.
